ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 9.8 GW of wind power, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 3.6 GW, representing 35.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Driven by this renewable volume, Scottish carbon intensity stands at an immaculate 0 gCO2/kWh, contrasting with the GB-wide level of 71 gCO2/kWh. However, cross-border transmission limits mean that low-carbon electricity cannot freely flow southward, resulting in severe grid constraints. So far today, 5,070 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed through Balancing Mechanism bids, accumulating a constraint cost of about £139,532. To replace this lost clean power, system operators were forced to dispatch fossil generation elsewhere, requiring an estimated 963,357 m3 of gas to be burned and adding 1,775 tonnes of CO2 to the atmosphere. Based on today's run-rate, the estimated total yearly cost of curtailment reaches £51 million to the nearest million. While these balancing actions ultimately filter down to end-users, calculating the exact £/MWh increase added to everybody's invoice across the UK cannot be performed without introducing total national consumption figures, which are excluded here to strictly avoid inventing unprovided data.
